# AudioView, MediaView and the media port

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The sound player component and the media port (video is `MediaView`, planned).

## `audioview`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/audioview.rs`)

`AudioView`: a sound player as a component an SDK app places in its layout (docs/development/UI-SDK.md, "Embedding audio and video").
The app keeps an `AudioView` in its state, gives it the core's [`MediaPort`] and a base action number, and a rectangle to draw in. The
view owns what is on screen: the list of the person's sound files, the transport bar (play or pause, 10 seconds back and forward, a
seek bar, volume, mute, speed), the level meter, the track list and the approval card for a remote source. It draws through [`Canvas`],
so it works in the shell, in a browser or client (display list) and as a WASM tile, with the colours and size class of the host. The
sound itself is the core's: it is decoded there and plays through the core's mixer, so the person's volume, ducking under speech and the
sound doctor apply; the view never touches a byte of it.

What the app does, in four lines:
```text
event(Tick):   audio.tick()                                (lists the files once, then polls the core's events)
event(Action): if audio.owns(a) { audio.action(a) }        event(Key): if audio.key(k) { return }
view:          audio.draw(c, th, &metrics, rect)           start something yourself: audio.open(Source::Home(name), "Title")
```
Keys: Space plays or pauses, Left and Right move 5 seconds, Up and Down choose in the list, Enter plays the chosen file, `+` and `-`
change the volume, `m` mutes, `r` changes the speed, `n` and `p` go to the next and the previous file, Esc stops.


## `mediaview`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/mediaview.rs`)

`MediaView`: a sound and video player as a component an SDK app places in its layout (docs/development/UI-SDK.md, "Embedding audio and
video"). It is an [`AudioView`] with a picture: the video surface on top (the core's pictures, drawn letterboxed with [`Canvas::image`]),
the transport, the seek bar, the level meter, the track list and the files below it, or the picture alone with a control bar in full
screen. The core decodes the video and picks the picture that is due on the sound's clock; the view only draws the newest one it was
given, so a slow screen shows fewer pictures and never falls behind the sound.

What the app does is what [`AudioView`] asks, plus `f` for full screen:
```text
event(Tick):   media.tick()                                 event(Action): if media.owns(a) { media.action(a) }
event(Key):    if media.key(k) { return }                   view: media.draw(c, th, &metrics, rect)
```
Keys: those of the audio view, `f` full screen, Esc leaves full screen first and then stops the player. Tap the picture to play or pause.
Captions: the list of caption tracks is shown and chosen; the caption text itself is not drawn yet (the facet carries no text).

### const `ACTIONS`

How many action numbers a media view uses, from the base the app gave it.

```rust
pub const ACTIONS: u32 = audioview::ACTIONS + 8
```

## `media`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/media.rs`)

The media port: what an SDK app is handed so that it can embed an audio or video player (see [`crate::audioview::AudioView`]). The port is
the core's `media` facet seen from the app: the person's own media files, one session at a time, control and events. The app never gets
a byte of the sound or a path: the core decodes, the sound goes through the core's mixer (so volume, ducking and the sound doctor apply),
and the app only draws state, position and a level. [`MemMedia`] is the in-memory port for tests and the browser preview: a virtual
clock the test moves, and the same rules as the core (a remote source waits for the person, a live stream cannot be moved, one session).

### trait `MediaPort`

```rust
pub trait MediaPort
```

Methods:

- `fn list_home(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<Item>, MediaError>`: The sound (and video) files of the person's home folder.
- `fn open(&mut self, source: &Source, title: &str, autoplay: bool) -> Result<bool, MediaError>`: Open `source` in this app's one session (an earlier one is closed). `Ok(true)`: the person must allow it first.
- `fn decide(&mut self, allow: bool) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn play(&mut self) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn pause(&mut self) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn seek(&mut self, ms: u64) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn set_rate(&mut self, permille: u32) -> Result<(), MediaError>`: Speed in thousandths (1000 is normal; 500 to 2000).
- `fn set_volume(&mut self, percent: u32) -> Result<(), MediaError>`: This player's own volume, 0 to 100 percent.
- `fn set_mute(&mut self, mute: bool) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn select_track(&mut self, id: u32) -> Result<(), MediaError>`
- `fn poll(&mut self) -> Vec<Event>`: The events since the last call.
- `fn frame(&mut self, _after: u64) -> Result<Option<crate::canvas::Image>, MediaError>  // has a default`: The picture of a video that is due now when its `seq` is above `after` (RGBA, scaled by the core to a size that fits the display list); `None`: nothing new, or the source has no picture. A sound-only port keeps the default.
- `fn close(&mut self)`: Stop the sound and close the session.

### struct `MemMedia`

An in-memory player. Clone it before handing it to a view: the clone is the test's handle (`advance` moves the clock).

```rust
pub struct MemMedia
```

Methods:

- `pub fn new() -> MemMedia`
- `pub fn unavailable() -> MemMedia`: A port that has no player at all.
- `pub fn put_file(&self, name: &str, duration_ms: u64, video: bool)`
- `pub fn put_video(&self, name: &str, duration_ms: u64, fps: u32, w: u32, h: u32)`: A video file: it has a picture, `fps` of them a second, `w` x `h` pixels; picture `n` is a plain field whose red is `n`.
- `pub fn put_stream(&self, url: &str, duration_ms: Option<u64>)`: A stream address; `None`: a live stream.
- `pub fn refuse_next(&self, why: &str)`: The next `open` is refused with this sentence.
- `pub fn set_level(&self, l: u32)`: The level the meter reports while playing (0 to 1000).
- `pub fn advance(&self, ms: u64)`: Move the clock: a playing session advances by `ms` at its rate, reports position and level, and ends at its end.
- `pub fn calls(&self) -> Vec<String>`: The calls the view made, in order (`open home a.mp3`, `play`, `seek 5000`, ...).
- `pub fn position(&self) -> u64`
- `pub fn volume(&self) -> (u32, bool)`
- `pub fn rate(&self) -> u32`
- `pub fn add_tracks_for_test(&self)`: Tests: the open file gains a second audio track and a caption track (the core announces them with the file).
